title: THE HOOK
cues: This sandwich used to be for RICH PEOPLE.
Yeah. THAT sandwich. The one your mom threw in a plastic bag.

title: THE WEIRD BEGINNING
cues: Back in the late 1800s, peanut butter wasn’t even considered normal food. It was promoted as a health food!
And somehow, it became a delicacy for wealthy Americans. They were eating it with watercress, cheese, even PIMENTOS.

title: THE GENIUS COMBINATION
cues: In 1901, she published the earliest known recipe combining peanut paste with jelly.
Not grape jelly. Not strawberry. CURRANT or CRABAPPLE jelly.

title: THE TECHNOLOGY THAT CHANGED EVERYTHING
cues: Then the 1920s happened. Peanut butter got creamier, lasted longer, and became cheaper.
And somebody finally figured out how to sell bread PRE-SLICED.
Suddenly, you didn’t need a fancy tea room. You needed three ingredients and about thirty seconds.

title: THE SANDWICH GOES TO WAR
cues: Then World War Two came along. Peanut butter and jelly were both included in American military rations.
Cheap. Portable. Packed with energy. And when soldiers came home, the combination was already familiar.
Before long, PB&J was taking over American lunchboxes.

title: THE PAYOFF
cues: So this ridiculously simple sandwich went from fancy tea parties… to wartime rations… to practically every American childhood.
All because someone looked at peanut butter and thought…
You know what this needs? Fruit goo.
